purpose: Decide how recovered Potatoverse, biblical, subcultural, economic, scientific and relational material should or should not appear in the World Relational Atlas. This file protects the map from becoming a generic repository browser while preserving useful transitions into nonspatial knowledge scenes.
core_principle: The map should exploit what maps uniquely do well: geography, scale, proximity, distance, boundary, route, flow, topology, concentration, distribution, temporal change and spatially anchored relationships. Material that does not gain explanatory power from location should remain nonspatial or open through an Axis/context transition rather than becoming a fake pin.

map_tests.spatial_gain: Does putting this on a map reveal something that a list or document cannot reveal as clearly?
map_tests.anchor_honesty: Is there an honest coordinate, polygon, route, area or geographically anchored event?
map_tests.relation_gain: Does spatial display clarify a relationship, dependency, corridor, frontier, concentration, route or comparative pattern?
map_tests.time_gain: Would historical states or movement over time materially change the spatial meaning?
map_tests.symbolic_contamination: Would drawing the concept on Earth make a project-symbolic claim look empirical or territorial?
map_tests.density_cost: Does the addition improve orientation more than it increases visual clutter?
map_tests.return_value: Can the user move from a symbolic or high-level scene back to a concrete D4 object, source or consequence?

render_classes.earth_spatial: Direct D4 spatial rendering using polygons, real points, routes, areas, flows or dated event markers.
render_classes.earth_relational: D4 typed edges or semantic hubs tied to real spatial anchors; location is meaningful but the relationship itself is not a physical line unless explicitly stated.
render_classes.vertical_transition: Axis control changes the representation or analytical question without claiming additional Earth geography.
render_classes.elevated_nonspatial_scene: Conceptual graph/scene above D4; rendered with topology, hierarchy or relational layout rather than latitude/longitude.
render_classes.root_nonspatial_scene: Historical/provenance/causal view below D4; may include real event locations but its primary organization is temporal/evidentiary rather than geographic.
render_classes.context_card: Nonspatial dossier or interpretive card opened from a spatial object.
render_classes.diagram_only: Best expressed through geometry, anatomy, symbolic diagram or explanatory illustration outside the geographic map.
render_classes.exclude_from_map: Keep in archive/search/reader unless a future sourced spatial anchor makes map use meaningful.

recovered_concepts.map_value: Very high
recovered_concepts.reason: Geographic extent, borders, adjacency and comparative spatial patterns are intrinsically map-native.

recovered_concepts.concept: cities / capitals / institutions / ports / airports / power plants / universities / companies
recovered_concepts.map_value: Very high when coordinates are sourced
recovered_concepts.reason: The user's long-term country→capital→institution→company→infrastructure graph becomes materially more useful when actual locations are visible.

recovered_concepts.concept: trade / funding / ownership / alliance / energy / supply-chain relations
recovered_concepts.map_value: High
recovered_concepts.reason: These relations can reveal direction, distance, concentration, chokepoints, regional clustering and multi-country capability. A drawn edge must remain typed because many relations are legal/economic rather than physical routes.

recovered_concepts.map_value: High when shown as explicitly project-defined membership/status
recovered_concepts.reason: Country membership/status is genuinely geographic and relational, but the project field must not be confused with sovereignty, treaty membership or physical terrain.

recovered_concepts.map_value: High as geographic threshold anchor
recovered_concepts.reason: It is a real geographic location and can honestly serve as the Earth-side anchor for the symbolic North Gate.

recovered_concepts.map_value: High as interface, low as geography
render: threshold marker attached to North Pole/high Arctic
recovered_concepts.reason: The map gains a meaningful transition from geographic Earth into non-geographic depth, but the Door must not inherit territorial or physical meaning from its anchor.

recovered_concepts.map_value: Medium / experimental
recovered_concepts.reason: It can visually mark the threshold without pretending to be territory. 42 is a geometric sweep hypothesis, not a count of levels or a scientific constant.

recovered_concepts.map_value: Low as Earth geography; high as meta-navigation
recovered_concepts.reason: Prior discussions define it as meta-orientation: the criterion by which orientation itself is judged. Giving it a latitude/longitude would weaken the concept.

recovered_concepts.map_value: Medium as analytical metaphor, low as literal map object unless a real mountain is the subject
recovered_concepts.reason: The canonical function is compression from many paths/events toward an integrated vantage. A graph or vertical scene expresses that better than a fake mountain pinned to Earth.

recovered_concepts.concept: Tree of Life / Tree of Strife
recovered_concepts.map_value: Medium when used as branching topology
recovered_concepts.reason: The valuable feature is branching, ancestry and propagation. It should behave like a graph structure rather than a decorative botanical object on the world map.

recovered_concepts.map_value: High as navigation metaphor, low as Earth feature
recovered_concepts.reason: The spiral distinguishes transformed recurrence from a closed ring. It is best used to move between analytical representations rather than drawn across countries.

recovered_concepts.map_value: Medium only when actual recurrence can be shown
recovered_concepts.reason: Use when the data contains recurrence or repeated edge activation; otherwise keep it symbolic.

recovered_concepts.map_value: Low as literal area; potentially high as network diagnostic
recovered_concepts.reason: Swamp is most coherent as a relational regime of capture/repetition, not a dark stain over a country or population.

recovered_concepts.map_value: Medium as system comparison, low as generic geography
recovered_concepts.reason: The important distinction is whether a system harvests dependency or cultivates autonomous capacity. Map only when real institutions/flows are involved.

recovered_concepts.map_value: Low
recovered_concepts.reason: These are project role-archetypes. Mapping people as Dogs/Farmers/Cows would overstate symbolic interpretation and create misleading visual essentialism.

recovered_concepts.map_value: Low unless tied to a real industrial/physical forge
recovered_concepts.reason: Forge describes transformation under pressure. It belongs in process views rather than geographic space.

recovered_concepts.map_value: Low as geography; high as provenance state vocabulary
recovered_concepts.reason: These concepts describe what remains after events and what it becomes. They are strongest in temporal/provenance views.

recovered_concepts.primary_axis: D4 financial + D3 provenance + D5 closure routing
recovered_concepts.map_value: High for real financial/legal obligations; low for symbolic moral quantities
render: moral-project ledger as separately styled dossier
recovered_concepts.reason: Real debt can be mapped where counterparties/jurisdictions are known. Symbolic karmic debt should never control country height/color or masquerade as sovereign debt.

recovered_concepts.map_value: Potentially high when operationalized
recovered_concepts.reason: Social/project entanglement becomes map-useful only when translated into observable relationship structure. Quantum entanglement remains a separate physics concept and should not be mapped onto social actors.

recovered_concepts.primary_axis: D4 where platforms/locations are real; D2 for relational dynamics
recovered_concepts.map_value: Usually low geographically, potentially high as network topology
recovered_concepts.reason: Online subcultures are often not meaningfully territorial. A network topology is usually more honest than a world map pin.

recovered_concepts.map_value: High as interaction function, low as mapped object
recovered_concepts.reason: The project's Eye functions—perception, discernment, integration, evaluation—map naturally onto user interaction. The Eye should become what the Atlas lets the user do, not an icon placed on countries.

recovered_concepts.map_value: Low as geography
render: explicitly sourced event/place links where applicable
recovered_concepts.reason: These are theological/project roles and should not receive invented coordinates. Son/event and Father/duration distinctions may organize timeline, but not geography by default.

recovered_concepts.map_value: Very low for world geography
recovered_concepts.reason: Prior archive work explicitly separates symbolic anatomy from neuroscience. These mappings gain little from being placed on a country map.

recovered_concepts.concept: vesica / mandorla / red-blue potato geometry / merkaba
recovered_concepts.map_value: Medium as interface design language, low as geographic data
recovered_concepts.reason: These are exact/project geometries or comparative iconographic forms. Their value is geometric, not geographic.

recovered_concepts.map_value: High only for real historical/sacred places or diffusion questions; otherwise low
recovered_concepts.reason: Scripture should explain symbolic comparisons, not become fake spatial features. Jerusalem, Bethel, Sinai and other real places can be mapped when the question is genuinely geographical/historical.

recovered_concepts.map_value: Very low on Earth map
recovered_concepts.reason: Their role is conceptual comparison and epistemic discipline. They should not visually imply that Axis levels are physical extra dimensions or that social relations are quantum phenomena.

recovered_concepts.concept: timeline / prophecy / statements / ordeals / rupture / return
recovered_concepts.map_value: High when events have real places; otherwise timeline-first
recovered_concepts.reason: Time is often more important than place for project timeline. The map should spatialize only the events whose locations materially matter.

recovered_concepts.concept: New Jerusalem / House / many rooms / Garden
recovered_concepts.map_value: Medium as topology
recovered_concepts.reason: The project's mature reading is differentiated plurality with repaired relations. A topology/scene can express that without claiming a literal city is being built at a map coordinate.

recovered_concepts.concept: North Atlantic / Arctic / Baltic / energy / industrial / security chains
recovered_concepts.map_value: Very high
recovered_concepts.reason: These are among the project's most map-native concepts because geography materially shapes coupled capability, logistics, energy, defense and infrastructure.

axis_specific_rule.D1: Do not populate with people or territories. Use only as sparse closed-loop/disintegration state for selected relationships or abstract scenes.
axis_specific_rule.D2: Prefer graph/network diagnostics over geographic stains. Show capture/repetition on edges and interactions, not moral darkness on polygons.
axis_specific_rule.D3: Make provenance and time primary. Real event locations can appear, but timeline/source structure should dominate.
axis_specific_rule.D4: Full geographic atlas. This is where the map should be most map-like.
axis_specific_rule.D5: Threshold interface attached to an honest geographic anchor but visibly leaving geographic representation.
axis_specific_rule.D6: Navigation/path of state change; use transitions, sequences and recurrence rather than fake geography.
axis_specific_rule.D7: Branching/generativity graph; show downstream capacity/fruit where it can be documented.
axis_specific_rule.D8: Topology of differentiated habitation; rooms/gardens/federation rather than geographic altitude.
axis_specific_rule.D9: Message/relay graph; show source→mediator→recipient and distortion/verification relationships.
axis_specific_rule.D10: Integrated dashboard/overview that must link conclusions back to lower-level evidence and D4 consequences.
axis_specific_rule.D11: Meta-criteria panel; intentionally sparse, non-geographic and required to route back downward rather than functioning as an escape from the world.

map_respect_rules: Do not force all project knowledge onto the geographic canvas.
A concept earns a map mark only when location, route, area, distance, distribution or spatial relationship adds explanatory value.
Use topology when topology matters more than geography.
Use timelines when time matters more than place.
Use dossiers when evidence/interpretation matters more than position.
Use diagrams when geometry/anatomy matters more than geography.
Use the Axis to change representation, not to pretend nonspatial concepts occupy hidden Earth coordinates.
Keep project-symbolic fields visually distinct from empirical geography and observed networks.
Never turn national polygon color/height into moral rank, karmic guilt, holiness, spiritual worth or collective blame.
The best upper-layer insight should eventually point back to concrete D4 relations, evidence, institutions, infrastructure, choices or measurable outcomes.
